Container.Name: textymcspeechy-piper
Container.Overview: TextyMcSpeechy trains custom Piper text-to-speech voices from your own recordings or any voice dataset, fully offline. The finished .onnx voices work with Home Assistant.[br][br] [b]This is not a web app.[/b] This container is the Piper training engine; it idles until the TextyMcSpeechy scripts (run from the Unraid terminal) send it work. You clone the TextyMcSpeechy repo onto your server and map its tts_dojo folder here. See the nelsonizedunraid README for the full Unraid setup.[br][br] [b]Requirements:[/b] an NVIDIA GPU and the Nvidia Driver plugin from Community Applications. The image is about 6 GB to download and over 10 GB on disk; plan on 50 GB+ free for checkpoints.[br][br] The WebUI link opens TensorBoard on port 6006, which only answers while a training session is running.
Container.Requires: An NVIDIA GPU with the Nvidia Driver plugin installed, and the TextyMcSpeechy repo cloned on the server (see the nelsonizedunraid README).

Config.Name: TTS Dojo
Config.Description: The tts_dojo folder inside your clone of the TextyMcSpeechy repo. Datasets, pretrained checkpoints, training runs and finished voices all live here.

Config.Name: TensorBoard Port
Config.Description: TensorBoard training graphs. Only active while training.

Config.Name: NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES
Config.Description: 'all', or the GPU UUID from the Nvidia Driver plugin page to pin one card.
